text:
sam: Heads up 1: new hire Olivia's EAD renewal is still pending; current EAD expires 5/3 and USCIS case receipt shows "Case was received" but no biometrics yet. She asked whether benefits will lapse.

olivia: I'm worried 1: wife is due in June and I need coverage. Did we ever allow special enrollments when EAD delayed but receipt exists?

jordan: Short answer: benefits are linked to payroll status. If she can't be added to payroll because the EAD is expired at the time of hire, enrollment won't activate until we confirm work authorization.

diego: One nuance: if she has a pending I-765 with a receipt notice (I-797C) and an expired EAD, some insurers accept the receipt for temporary coverage depending on carrier rules. Not universal. We need carrier confirmation.

peopleops-bot: Quick checklist posted: bring copy of I-797C receipt, copy of expiring EAD front/back, any USCIS biometrics notice. Contact benefits@redwood for carrier-specific exceptions.

sam: Can payroll create a provisional record while we wait for EAD? Manager is ok to start on 5/1.

payroll-team: We can queue a hire record but cannot process pay until I-9 passes with valid document combo. For I-9, an unexpired EAD OR List B + List C combos are needed. A receipt alone doesn't satisfy the I-9.

jordan: We should offer two paths: 1) start date delayed until EAD is in hand (on-payroll), or 2) unpaid onboarding until EAD arrives. Plus we can ask carriers about bridging coverage.

olivia: Is there any reason we couldn't do a "contingent start" with laptop/training but unpaid? I don't want to lose the offer.

sam: Manager prefers option 2 (unpaid onboarding week and manager-approved learning plan). We'll document in an offer addendum.

diego: I'll call our main medical carrier rep to ask about provisional coverage with I-797C. If they say yes, we'll need to submit receipt copies and coordinator statement. That can take 3-5 business days.

payroll-team: Also, immigration note: if the EAD renewal is pending but the current EAD is expired at start date, IRS/tax withholding still allowed when on payroll but we can't legally employ without authorization. So must not do paid work.

jordan: HR action items: 1) prepare short offer addendum for unpaid onboarding and equipment loaner policy; 2) draft consent request to carrier for provisional coverage; 3) advise manager on what tasks are allowed (no billable code reviews, only orientation).

peopleops-bot: Template addendum: "Start date contingent on valid work authorization. Pre-start training permitted unpaid. Employee will be added to payroll on receipt of acceptable I-9 documents." Will DM.

olivia: Thank you all 1: appreciate the help. Please share carrier update when you have it. I can upload my receipt and biometrics notice to the secure HR folder.

diego: Will update here once I hear back from carrier. If they accept receipt as temporary proof we'll attempt to enroll retroactively to the requested date, pending carrier approval.

sam: Closing the loop 1: manager approves unpaid onboarding starting 5/1. Olivia, please upload scanned receipt + biometrics notice to the HR upload link and confirm. We'll reconvene after carrier response.

peopleops-bot: Reminder: if anyone needs the secure upload link, ping peopleops-bot DM and it will provide SSO link.

olivia: Uploaded receipts just now. Thanks.

jordan: Noted. Payroll will stand by to create employee record once docs are acceptable.

diego: Carrier responded: they require active EAD for enrollment, no bridging allowed. I'll send the rep's email thread and next steps for COBRA/short-term alternatives.

sam: Thanks Diego. We'll offer short-term options (spouse's plan, marketplace, or short-term medical) and reimburse relocation/medical expenses per policy if approved by manager.

olivia: Understood. Please keep me posted on reimbursement policies.

sam: Will do. End thread.
